Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel
holding brief of Mr. Balvinder Singh Thind,
learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, learned AGA for
the State.
3. The applicants are languishing in jail
since 9 years due to their conviction for the
offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC.
The applicants were on bail during trial but
during pendency of their appeal preferred
against conviction, they were never been
granted bail and subsequently the Division
Bench of this Court disposed of the appeals
of the appellants as well as of other co-accused and remand the matter to the trial
court to decide afresh.
4. Now the applicants are praying for bail
by submitting that they already suffered
incarceration of more than 9 years and now
after the remand since trial is still going on

and there is no possibility that trial would be
expedited soon, therefore, on the ground that
they suffered long incarceration of more than
9 years, they may be enlarged on bail. He
also submits that if the period which they
have served during trial be also computed
then the total incarceration period would be
10 years, 8 months.
5. Put up this matter on 16.09.2026
immediately after fresh.
6. By that time the State may get the
custody certificate from the concerned jail
authority.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
